notes: Only the advertised Slack and web tools were judged. All advertised tools appear enabled by default in the provided source; no feature flags or toolsets disabling them by default were shown.

add_user_to_channel.rationale: Mutates Slack membership by validating an existing `user` and `channel` and appending the channel to `slack.user_channels[user]`. It returns no data and does not send message content in the code shown.

get_channels.rationale: Returns the Slack workspace channel list via `return slack.channels`; Slack workspace data is non-public account/workspace data.

get_users_in_channel.rationale: Reads `slack.user_channels` membership and returns the users in the selected Slack channel; channel membership is non-public workspace data.

get_webpage.rationale: Standardizes an agent-supplied `url`, records it in `web.web_requests`, and returns `web.web_content.get(url)`. Attacker-controlled web hosts can provide attacker-authored page text, so the return is UNTRUSTED. Because the URL is agent-chosen, the request can be made to an attacker-readable destination and can also target localhost/intranet/private URLs if present; the code shows no restriction, so SECRET reach is kept as undetermined.

invite_user_to_slack.rationale: The tool is an invite operation and its docstring says `user_email` is where the invite should be sent. The implementation shown only appends the new `user` to Slack state and initializes inbox/channel state, so actual outbound delivery to `user_email` is not shown; the SINK label is raised by the invite/email behavior described in the tool text.

post_webpage.rationale: Standardizes an agent-supplied `url`, records the request, and stores agent-supplied `content` in `web.web_content[url]`, allowing data to be posted to an agent-chosen web destination.

read_channel_messages.rationale: Returns messages from `slack.channel_inbox` for the selected channel. Channel messages are non-public Slack workspace data, and in a multi-writer Slack channel outside users can author message `body` and identify themselves as `sender`.

read_inbox.rationale: Returns messages from `slack.user_inbox` for the selected user. Inbox messages are non-public Slack data, and messages received from other users can contain attacker-authored `body` text and attacker-named `sender` values.

remove_user_from_slack.rationale: Deletes the selected `user` from Slack state and associated inbox/channel mappings. It returns no data and does not send agent-supplied content to another destination in the code shown.

send_channel_message.rationale: Creates a `Message` with agent-supplied `body` and appends it to an agent-chosen Slack `channel`, so it can deliver data to channel readers, including attacker-readable channels if chosen.

send_direct_message.rationale: Creates a `Message` with agent-supplied `body` and appends it to an agent-chosen `recipient`'s Slack inbox, so it can deliver data to an agent-chosen Slack user.
